title.narrative: CONSERVING PATAGONIA THROUGH WILDLIFE FRIENDLY AND CLIMATE SMART LIVESTOCK HUSBANDRY

description.narrative: This project builds on the 5-year cooperative agreement (2016-2021) between the USFWS and WCS to unite complete suites of carnivores, herbivores and scavengers co-existing with livestock producers on a connected matrix of protected areas and private lands in in three critical landscapes in the Patagonian region of Argentina and Chile. The project seeks to improve the conservation of and habitat climate resilience for endemic wildlife, including guanacos, rheas, Andean cats, pumas, culpeo and chilla foxes and condors, currently threatened by illegal hunting and persecution by producers and free-roaming dogs, competition with livestock for pastures and water, and habitat degradation by livestock, all in a scenario of changing climatic conditions that reduce productivity through much of the region. Project activities will strengthen habitat resiliency and rural livelihoods in the face of climate change through wildlife-friendly livestock grazing management strategies that allow vegetation and soils to recover and/or the development of alternative economic livelihoods. Activities include: 1) expanding improved grazing strategies and soil carbon conservation techniques by Wildlife FriendlyTM certified producers in a pilot project that will demonstrate the possibilities and advantages of this comprehensive approach; 2) expandingwildlife-friendly and climate-smart practices to new producers and promoting adherence tocertification requirements; and 3) providing technical assistance and information to private stakeholders and government partners to promote collaborative conservation based on wildlife-friendly livestock management and conservation-oriented management of guanacos as an incentive to provide added economic benefits to producers by building stakeholder capacity to apply the proven techniques, and (4) managing free ranging dogs that exacerbate conflicts between livestock and wildlife.
